messages:
carl: heads up — planning a rolling reboot for 02:00–04:00 UTC tonight targeting shared GPU pool racks in us-east1 (rack-14 and rack-15). doing interleaved drains to avoid >15% capacity loss in any AZ. canary at 02:10 on rack-14a. expect short-lived burst capacity drop and a few elevated tail latencies.

mina: will this touch Dedicated pools or any pinned capacity? SLA concerns from enterprise customers.

carl: Dedicated/reserved pools are NOT impacted — this is limited to the shared 'saturn' pool. enterprise SLAs should remain intact. we'll keep routing + canary traffic away from affected racks using our placement policy.

devon: what's the backfill plan? if we spin up spot capacity to backfill, cost could spike. any estimate?

carl: backfill will use warm standby spot nodes in us-east1-burst and cross-zone burst if needed. estimate ~ $1.5k–2.5k for the window (short ramp). will tag infra with `maint/apr-rolling-14` so finance can reconcile.

aj: can we lower model footprint temporarily? e.g. auto-fallback to quantized-8bit variants or shorter max_length for non-critical traffic?

carl: yes — we'll enable routing policy fallback to `model-quant-v2` for non-SL tier routes and decrease default max_tokens to 512 for the window. ops script below to cordon/drain/reboot/uncordon:

```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-node-14a
kubectl drain gpu-node-14a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# reboot
ssh node-14a 'sudo systemctl reboot'
# post-check
kubectl uncordon gpu-node-14a
./scripts/check-pod-liveness --rack rack-14a
```

devon: we should also seed KV/prefix cache after the node comes back to avoid high token cost from cold runs. any seed script?

carl: yep — running this after uncordon: `python infra/seed_cache.py --rack rack-14a --prefixes 2000 --concurrency 8`. also kicking an automated warmup job that primes common prefixes for top-10 tenant prompts.

mina: how are we communicating to customers? support + account execs need a brief to forward.

carl: emailing support/product now. support ticket template: short outage window, affected pool (shared saturn), expected risk (brief latency spike), rollback plan. posting public status message only if we see customer-impact >10 min.

sre-bot: scheduled event created: `maintenance/1777778888-rolling-reboot-us-east1` — reminder at 01:45 UTC. alerting: silencing non-critical latency alerts for saturn pool from 01:50–04:15 UTC.

aj: will tracing/console be toggled for extra visibility? we should increase sampling for the canary traffic.

carl: yes — ramp tracing to 20% for canary racks and enable per-route latency dashboards. if tail > 500ms for >5m, we abort and roll back.

mina: ack :thumbsup:

devon: ack, will standby to flip fallback if needed :eyes:

carl: thanks — ping me here if you see anything odd. will post a short ops wrap after the window.
